content:
The image shows a corn stalk cross-section/surface with:
- Tan/straw-colored stalk tissue background
- Dense scattering of tiny black dots (microsclerotia) across the entire surface
- No large lesions, no mycelial growth, just uniformly distributed minute black specks

The key diagnostic feature here is the countless tiny black microsclerotia peppered across the tan stalk tissue. This is the hallmark of **Charcoal stalk rot** (*Macrophomina phaseolina*), where the fungus produces abundant microsclerotia that appear as a "pepper-and-salt" pattern on the internal stalk tissue. The tan/gray-brown background with black speckling is exactly what distinguishes charcoal rot from other stalk rots (Diplodia has white mycelium, Anthracnose has shiny black acervuli on darker tissue, Fusarium shows pink/white discoloration).
